candidate.title: System 1 & 2 in AI: Latent Reasoning Between Fast and Slow Thinking
candidate.description:
How do large language models balance intuition and deliberation—the so-called System 1 and System 2 of human cognition?
This video breaks down Meta & TUM’s new paper “Exploring System 1 and 2 Communication for Latent Reasoning in LLMs” (Coda-Forno et al., 2025).

🧩 Key ideas covered:

The concept of dual-architecture latent reasoning, where a Base model (System 1) communicates with a Coprocessor (System 2).

Two hypotheses for improving “latent communication”:

Frozen-Base KV augmentation – extending the model’s cache to carry richer latent signals.

Co-finetuning – training both modules jointly to let the Base “listen” to System 2.

Comparison with soft-embedding baselines, showing that current dual systems mostly add compute rather than qualitatively new reasoning.

Results on GSM8K, ProsQA, and a “Countdown” reasoning stress test.

Why LLMs may still lack true System 2-like planning—and what future objectives might fix that.

📘 Paper: arXiv:2510.00494

📚 Authors: Julian Coda-Forno et al., Meta AI & Helmholtz Munich (2025)
